title: Chrome Extension × WebMCP × AI Usage Skill Visualizer
about_excerpt: Human Focus in AI. Like Comment Story Updates AI Usage Skill Visualizer — WebMCP Challenge Edition WebMCP E2E workflow completed with PDF generation and reverse handoff Evaluation result with 438/500 score, PDF generation, and successful reverse handoff Generated AI Usage Report with an overall score of 438/500 Chrome extension extracting the ChatGPT conversation log for evaluation Inspiration This project started with a question about my own use of AI. During a conversation with AI, it pointed out something about the way I was using it. That made me wonder: How well am I actually using AI? Then another question came to mind: Isn't everyone using AI in more or less the same way? And if not: What is the difference? That was the starting point for visualizing human AI usage skills. By that time, I had already been using AI for more than two years. Because of that experience, it felt natural to me that the final output alone could not tell you how well someone had used AI. If I wanted to understand how a person used AI, I also needed to look at the conversation process that led to the final result. So the idea was to evaluate the conversation log, the final output, and the relationship between them. That became the foundation of AI Usage Skill Visualizer. As I continued developing it, I noticed something else. Knowing whether someone uses AI, or how much they use it, is not the same as understanding how well they can actually use it. And knowing about AI is not the same as being able to use AI effectively in real work. AI Usage Tracking ≠ AI Usage Skill AI Knowledge ≠ Practical AI Capability From the beginning, the concept was also broader than just building a standalone evaluation application. I wanted to connect the whole process: Use AI → Capture the interaction process → Evaluate human AI usage → Visualize the result → Return the result to the AI workflow At the time, however, I did not have a practical way to directly connect the environment where people were actually using AI with the Visualizer. So I started with what I could actually implement at the time: a standalone application. The first approach was simple. Users manually entered their conversation logs and outputs, and the Visualizer evaluated them. But once I started using it myself, I realized that this manual input process was more cumbersome than I had expected. To reduce that friction, I built a Chrome extension that could bring ChatGPT conversations into the Visualizer. That made the process of importing conversation logs much simpler. There was still another gap between the AI workflow and the Visualizer. This is where WebMCP changed what was possible. Using WebMCP Site Tools, the AI workflow can directly use the Visualizer's capabilities to run the evaluation, generate a PDF report, and read the generated report back into the workflow. By combining that with the Chrome extension and reverse handoff, I was also able to return the evaluation result to the original ChatGPT conversation. The Challenge Edition demonstrates this flow: Chrome Extension × WebMCP × AI Usage Skill Visualizer → Evaluation → PDF Report → Reverse Handoff → ChatGPT Summary WebMCP was not something I added afterward simply because this was a WebMCP Challenge. From the beginning of the idea, I wanted to connect everything from using AI, to evaluating how it was used, to returning the result back to the AI workflow. Using WebMCP finally allowed me to move closer to that original concept in a practical way. Human Focus in AI. What it does AI Usage Skill Visualizer — WebMCP Edition is a Challenge-specific implementation that demonstrates how WebMCP can connect an AI interaction directly to AI usage evaluation. The project combines: Chrome Extension × WebMCP × AI Usage Skill Visualizer The Chrome extension can extract a ChatGPT conversation and provide a path for that conversation to become Visualizer input. For the public Challenge demo, the built-in public sample data is used so that the evaluation workflow can be reproduced consistently. The user starts the analysis from AI Usage Skill Visualizer. From there, Work uses WebMCP Site Tools to continue the workflow. The WebMCP workflow can: receive the conversation log and final output run the Challenge-specific evaluation return structured evaluation results generate a PDF report read the generated report back into the workflow After the evaluation and report workflow are complete, the result is prepared for reverse handoff. The Chrome extension then returns the evaluation prompt to the original Chrome ChatGPT conversation. The extension: identifies the target ChatGPT conversation receives the evaluation payload finds the ChatGPT composer inserts the evaluation prompt verifies the inserted text It deliberately does not click Send or simulate Enter. The final submission remains under human control. After the user manually sends the prompt, ChatGPT summarizes the evaluation inside the original conversation. The complete demonstration flow is: Chrome Extension → WebMCP → AI Usage Skill Visualizer → Evaluation → PDF Report → Reverse Handoff → ChatGPT Summary The Challenge Edition uses deterministic evaluation logic created specifically for this public demonstration. It is intentionally separate from the production AI Usage Skill Visualizer evaluation engine. The important part of this Challenge project is not the simplified score itself. The important part is that WebMCP turns the Visualizer from a separate destination into something that can participate directly in an AI workflow. How we built it I built the WebMCP Challenge Edition as a separate implementation from the production AI Usage Skill Visualizer. The Challenge application uses a lightweight web interface built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, together with a local backend for report generation and supporting the end-to-end workflow. The application exposes WebMCP Site Tools that can be discovered and called from Work. The main tools are: evaluate_ai_usage_demo This tool receives structured evaluation input including: conversation_log output It then: receives the submitted conversation log and output displays them in the Visualizer runs the Challenge-specific deterministic evaluation renders the evaluation result returns structured evaluation data through WebMCP create_ai_usage_report This tool receives the evaluation result and generates the PDF report used by the Challenge workflow. The generated PDF is not only a UI result. It becomes a real workflow artifact that can be passed to the next stage. read_generated_report This tool reads the generated report back into the workflow so that Work can verify the result and continue the process. Together, these Site Tools allow Work to move from structured input through evaluation and report generation without requiring the user to manually transfer intermediate results between each stage.
